component.name: Signet
component.summary: Keep OpenPGP keys in an encrypted vault

description.p: Signet stores OpenPGP keys in a KeePass vault and asks before signing or decrypting. Use your keys with GnuPG and Git while keeping secret key material inside the encrypted vault.
Create a vault, open an existing file, or download one from WebDAV. Import keys, share public certificates, and sync the same vault with Signet for Android.
Signet locks after an idle period and lets you approve each use of a key. The app runs in the background after its window closes.

screenshot.caption: Manage OpenPGP keys in your encrypted vault

description.p: Manage Subkeys in a key's details adds Ed25519, Cv25519 and RSA subkeys, changes expiry dates, revokes and deletes subkeys, and attaches a key from another key in the vault as a subkey, keeping its fingerprint so old mail still decrypts.

Subkeys deleted in Signet or on another device are now removed from GnuPG too. After turning on the standard GnuPG home, Signet explains that Flatpak mail apps such as Evolution need access to GnuPG's socket folder.

Signet can serve GnuPG's standard home, so programs find it without setting GNUPGHOME. The signing and decryption prompts can be turned off separately, a native install names Flatpak apps and remembers approvals for each, and secret keys can be exported as a passphrase-protected backup.
Importing a key now reports a wrong passphrase as such, and GnuPG Ed25519 keys exported without a passphrase whose secret starts with a zero byte import completely.
Setting up GnuPG before any key is imported no longer fails, and GnuPG errors now include GnuPG's own message.
